_source.description: Major global hafnium production and processing sites — byproduct of zirconium refining
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); Orano/Framatome corporate reports; ATI (Allegheny Technologies) SEC filings and annual reports; CNNC (China National Nuclear Corporation) reports; Nuclear Fuel Complex India publications; Chepetsky Mechanical Plant (TVEL/Rosatom) data; KEPCO Nuclear Fuel annual reports; Australian Strategic Materials (ASM) ASX filings
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary
_source.notes: Hafnium is produced exclusively as a byproduct of nuclear-grade zirconium refining (separation of Hf from Zr). Global production estimated at ~70 tonnes/year. Supply is highly concentrated — France (Orano/Framatome CEZUS), USA (ATI), and China (CNNC) account for the majority. Used in nuclear reactor control rods, superalloys (jet engines), semiconductor gate insulators (HfO2), and plasma cutting tips. Designated a USGS critical mineral. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company filings, and satellite verification. Capacity figures are estimates based on published production data and industry reports; exact plant-level hafnium output is often proprietary.

sites.name: CEZUS/Framatome Zirconium Plant (Jarrie)
sites.notes: Primary Western world hafnium producer. CEZUS Jarrie plant performs Zr/Hf separation via liquid-liquid extraction (Malouf process). Supplies nuclear-grade hafnium for French and export reactor programs. Largest single hafnium production site globally.

sites.name: CEZUS Paimboeuf Plant
sites.notes: Secondary CEZUS facility near mouth of Loire; handles zirconium/hafnium processing and fabrication. Produces hafnium metal products for aerospace and nuclear applications.

sites.name: ATI Specialty Alloys and Components (Albany)
sites.notes: Primary US hafnium producer. Albany, Oregon facility (formerly Wah Chang/Teledyne) has produced reactor-grade zirconium and hafnium since the 1950s. Kroll process reduction of HfCl4 to hafnium metal sponge. Supplies US Navy nuclear propulsion program.

sites.name: Western Zirconium (Westinghouse)
sites.notes: Ogden, Utah facility produces nuclear-grade zirconium alloy tubing (Zircaloy) for fuel cladding. Hafnium separated as byproduct; used in reactor control rods. Supplies Westinghouse fuel fabrication plants.

sites.name: CNNC Nuclear Grade Zirconium Plant (Baoji)
sites.notes: Baoji, Shaanxi Province. Primary Chinese nuclear-grade Zr/Hf separation facility. Supplies hafnium for China's expanding nuclear reactor fleet (Hualong One, CAP1400 programs). Part of CNNC's nuclear fuel cycle infrastructure.

sites.name: Guangdong Orient Zirconic (Foshan)
sites.operator: Guangdong Orient Zirconic Industry Science & Technology
sites.notes: Foshan, Guangdong Province. Produces zirconium chemicals and zirconia products with hafnium as byproduct. One of China's largest zirconium processors by volume, though mainly industrial-grade rather than nuclear-grade.

sites.name: State Nuclear Bao-Ti Zirconium (Baoji)
sites.operator: State Nuclear Bao-Ti Zirconium Industry Co.
sites.notes: Baoji, Shaanxi Province. Joint venture between state nuclear entities and Baoji Titanium Industry (BaoTi). Produces nuclear-grade zirconium sponge and hafnium byproduct for China's domestic reactor construction program.

sites.name: Nuclear Fuel Complex (Hyderabad)
sites.ownership: Government of India, Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)
sites.notes: Hyderabad, Telangana. India's sole Zr/Hf separation facility under the Department of Atomic Energy. Produces zirconium alloy fuel cladding for India's PHWR (pressurized heavy water reactor) fleet. Hafnium used in Indian nuclear reactor control assemblies.

sites.name: Indian Rare Earths Zircon Processing (Kerala)
sites.notes: Chavara/Manavalakurichi, Kerala coast. IREL processes beach sand heavy minerals including zircon (ZrSiO4) which contains ~1-2% Hf. Zircon concentrate sent to NFC Hyderabad for Zr/Hf separation. Feeds India's nuclear fuel cycle.

sites.name: Chepetsky Mechanical Plant (Glazov)
sites.notes: Glazov, Udmurt Republic. Russia's primary zirconium/hafnium production facility under Rosatom's TVEL subsidiary. Produces nuclear-grade Zr alloys (E110, E635) and hafnium metal for VVER reactor control elements. Also processes depleted uranium and calcium.

sites.name: Hokkaido Zr/Hf Separation Facility
sites.operator: Nuclear Fuel Industries (NFI) / Sumitomo Metal Mining
sites.notes: Tomakomai, Hokkaido. Japanese Zr/Hf separation for domestic nuclear fuel fabrication. Most Japanese hafnium demand met by imports from France (CEZUS) and USA (ATI); domestic separation is supplementary.

sites.name: Dnipro Zirconium Plant (PChZ)
sites.operator: SE Vilnohirsk Mining and Metallurgical Plant (VSMMP)
sites.ownership: Ukrainian state (National Nuclear Energy Generating Company Energoatom supply chain)
sites.notes: Dnipro (Dnipropetrovsk) region. Produces zirconium products for Ukraine's VVER-1000 reactors with hafnium as byproduct. Part of Ukraine's effort to reduce dependence on Russian nuclear fuel supply chain. Operations impacted by ongoing conflict since 2022.

sites.name: KEPCO Nuclear Fuel (Daejeon)
sites.ownership: KEPCO (Korea Electric Power Corporation, Korean state majority)
sites.notes: Daejeon, South Korea. Fabricates nuclear fuel assemblies for Korea's PWR fleet. Imports zirconium/hafnium feedstock; performs some domestic Zr/Hf processing. Hafnium used in control rod components for Korean Standard Nuclear Plants (KSNP).

sites.name: INB Zirconium Processing
sites.notes: Resende, Rio de Janeiro state. INB processes zirconium for fuel assemblies used in Brazil's Angra 1 and Angra 2 PWR reactors. Hafnium separated as byproduct. Small-scale production supporting domestic nuclear program.

sites.name: ANSTO/Alkane Hafnium Project (pending)
sites.ownership: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) in partnership with ANSTO (Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation)
sites.notes: Proposed European processing facility for hafnium/zirconium from Alkane's Dubbo polymetallic project (Australia). ANSTO developed proprietary separation technology. Location under evaluation; Germany among candidate sites for downstream processing.

sites.name: Dubbo Project (Australian Strategic Materials)
sites.notes: Toongi deposit near Dubbo, NSW. Polymetallic alkaline intrusive containing zirconium, hafnium, niobium, and rare earth elements. ANSTO-developed hydrometallurgical flowsheet for Zr/Hf separation. DFS completed; seeking project financing. Could become significant non-Chinese hafnium source.

sites.name: Teck Trail Operations (Zr/Hf processing)
sites.notes: Trail, British Columbia. Teck's integrated metallurgical complex processes various specialty metals. Limited zirconium/hafnium processing as part of diversified operations. Minor producer; primarily a zinc-lead smelter with specialty metals recovery.

sites.name: Sandvik Zirconium Processing (Sandviken)
sites.notes: Sandviken, Sweden. Sandvik produces zirconium alloy tubing for nuclear fuel cladding (SANDVIK Zircaloy). Hafnium handled as byproduct of tube manufacturing process. Supplies European nuclear utilities.
